d: The most fundamental data structures. Arrays provide O(1) access but O(n) insertion/deletion in the middle.

p: Arrays are contiguous blocks of memory. Because they are contiguous, accessing any element by index is instantaneous. However, inserting or deleting an element in the middle requires shifting all subsequent elements.
Dynamic Arrays (like Python List or Java ArrayList) allocate a fixed size under the hood.
When full, they allocate a new array of double the size and copy elements over (Amortized O(1)).

arr = [1, 2, 3]
arr.append(4) # Amortized O(1)
arr.insert(0, 0) # O(N) because elements shift

# String concatenation in loops is bad:
s = ""
for char in chars:
  s += char # O(N^2) in Java/C++
# Use join instead:
s = "".join(chars) # O(N)
Time: O(1) read/write, O(N) insert/delete. Space: O(N) for dynamic resizing.

Memory Layout:
[Index 0] [Index 1] [Index 2] [Index 3]
| 0x1000  | 0x1004  | 0x1008  | 0x100C  |
O(1) access because Address = Base + (Index * Size)
